name: Refugee Status Determination

requirements.blocker_text: Law No. 44 'On Refugees' (2002, amended 2006 and 2016) is the legal basis; the Ministry of Labour, Social Security and Migration (MLSSM), through its Department for Work with Repatriates (Kayrylman) and Refugees, determines status. Applicants submit personal details and an explanation of the need for protection, in Kyrgyz or Russian; missing documents do not bar filing, and free legal support is available from the NGO Legal Clinic 'Adilet.' Applicants receive a 'Certificate of Registration of an Application for Refugee Status,' valid 3 months and renewable until a final decision, and must report their address to local Population Services Centers within 5 working days. Rejections may be appealed to court within 3 months.
requirements.fix_path: File a refugee status application with the MLSSM's Department for Work with Repatriates and Refugees, in Kyrgyz or Russian; free legal assistance is available from the NGO Legal Clinic 'Adilet.'

evidence_required.document: Identity documentation (if available -- missing documents do not bar filing)

outcome.duration_length: indefinite for recognized refugees; provisional certificate renewable every 3 months pending determination

sources.title: UNHCR Central Asia -- asylum process in the Kyrgyz Republic: MLSSM determination, registration certificate, appeal deadlines, refugee rights (work, movement, education, property, civil registration)

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Kyrgyzstan). STATUS: DRAFT -- tier 2 (a UNHCR operational page describing the Kyrgyz government's own process; this dataset attempted to fetch the actual Law 44/2002 text twice, both directly from Refworld and from the Kyrgyz Ministry of Justice's own legal database (cbd.minjust.gov.kg), but both returned only metadata, not substantive article text -- a genuine, disclosed fetch gap, not a claim the law doesn't exist). GENUINE, UNUSUALLY CONCRETE POSITIVE FINDING: this is among the most generous and specific refugee-rights lists found in this entire dataset -- recognized refugees may work WITHOUT a separate permit and start businesses, travel freely, access public healthcare and full education, register births/marriages, and hold limited property-purchase rights, with concrete deadlines throughout the process (3-month certificate renewal, 5-day address registration, 3-month appeal window, 7-day change-of-circumstances notification). work_rights/study_rights set to 'full' reflecting this explicit textual confirmation, a contrast to Mozambique, Angola, and Cameroon's refugee files earlier in this dataset, which all had to default to 'restricted' due to unconfirmed or disclosed-as-limited rights.
